governance: CANDIDATES ONLY — discovery is not trust. No row here is an active capability; each must pass the seeder's gap/lift screen, then human/eval gates, before any promotion. Source URLs are as reported; license/verify_note flags carried verbatim. serves_truth=false for everything downstream. Excludes already-seeded Firecrawl, dennisgl/mcp-playwright-scraper, and the official fetch server to avoid duplication.

candidates.intent: Drive a managed cloud browser (Browserbase + Stagehand) to navigate, click, fill forms, run JS, and extract structured data from dynamic pages.
candidates.input_contract: a target URL plus natural-language and/or coded interaction steps and an optional extraction schema
candidates.output_contract: extracted structured data, rendered page content, console logs, or screenshots
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A bare LLM cannot provision a real cloud browser, render JS-heavy SPAs, maintain a session, or interact with page elements.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds a hosted Stagehand-driven browser so the model can act on and read pages it otherwise cannot reach, with screenshots and console capture.
candidates.verify_note: Repo wraps Browserbase+Stagehand; requires a Browserbase API key. Wrapper license not confirmed on listing (Stagehand itself is MIT).

candidates.intent: Automate a browser with a mix of natural-language actions (act/extract/observe) and deterministic Playwright code.
candidates.input_contract: a page plus act/extract/observe instructions or explicit Playwright steps
candidates.output_contract: action results, extracted typed data, or observed page state
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A model alone cannot bridge between unreliable high-level agents and brittle hand-written selectors on unfamiliar pages.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds a framework that lets the agent choose code (deterministic) vs AI (adaptive) per step, raising reliability of web automation.
candidates.verify_note: MIT per repo; SDK requires an LLM + browser backend. Not itself an MCP server.

candidates.intent: Run thousands of ready-made Apify Actors (scrapers/crawlers) to extract data from social media, search engines, maps, e-commerce, or any website.
candidates.input_contract: an actor selection or search plus the actor's typed input (URLs, queries, filters)
candidates.output_contract: the actor's dataset output as structured records
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A model cannot operate site-specific scrapers, handle proxies/anti-bot, or paginate large crawls on its own.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds dynamic discovery and execution of a large library of maintained scrapers returning structured datasets with source handles.
candidates.verify_note: MIT per repo footer; requires an Apify token and per-actor costs. Output quality varies by actor.

candidates.intent: Let an AI agent complete multi-step web tasks (search, form-fill, navigation, extraction) by controlling a real browser via Playwright.
candidates.input_contract: a natural-language web task and target site(s)
candidates.output_contract: task result plus extracted data and an action trace
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A model cannot itself drive a browser through multi-step, stateful interactions without hand-written selectors.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds an LLM-driven Playwright agent that completes browsing workflows and returns extracted results; also exposes an MCP integration.
candidates.verify_note: MIT per repo; outcomes are model-dependent and non-deterministic — treat as a bounded agent behind a port, never a truth source.

candidates.intent: Crawl websites and convert pages into LLM-ready Markdown/structured output with content filtering and chunking.
candidates.input_contract: seed URL(s) plus crawl depth/filters and an optional extraction strategy
candidates.output_contract: cleaned Markdown or structured JSON per page with metadata
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A model cannot crawl, render, or strip boilerplate from many pages to produce clean retrieval-ready text.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds fast async crawling with content filtering and Markdown/JSON extraction tuned for LLM pipelines.
candidates.verify_note: Apache-2.0 with attribution clause per project; LLM-extraction strategies add model dependence on top of deterministic crawl.

candidates.intent: Build reliable crawlers with proxy rotation, request queues, and headful/headless browsing to download HTML/PDF/images for AI pipelines.
candidates.input_contract: start URLs, a request handler, and crawl configuration
candidates.output_contract: a dataset of extracted records plus downloaded files
candidates.gap_hypothesis: Stateful crawling (queues, retries, proxy rotation, anti-bot) is infrastructure a model cannot provide itself.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds a batteries-included crawling framework (Parsel/BeautifulSoup/Playwright) for robust large-scale extraction.
candidates.verify_note: License Apache-2.0 per Apify projects; confirm on repo LICENSE before relying.

candidates.intent: Run a high-throughput asynchronous crawling/scraping framework with selectors, pipelines, and middlewares.
candidates.input_contract: spider definition (start URLs, parse rules, item schema)
candidates.output_contract: structured items exported to JSON/CSV/JSONL
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A model has no async crawling engine, scheduling, or item-pipeline machinery to scrape at scale.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds a mature, deterministic crawling framework with pluggable extraction and export pipelines.
candidates.verify_note: BSD-3-Clause confirmed (PyPI SPDX). Maintained by Zyte.

candidates.intent: Drive a browser via structured accessibility snapshots (not screenshots) to navigate, fill forms, capture network, and manage storage.
candidates.input_contract: a target URL plus structured interaction steps
candidates.output_contract: accessibility snapshot, action results, screenshots, or network captures
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A model cannot render pages or read interactive element structure without a browser engine; screenshot-only approaches are lossy.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds Microsoft's official Playwright MCP that exposes accessibility-tree snapshots, bypassing vision models for reliable element targeting.
candidates.verify_note: Official Microsoft repo; Playwright is Apache-2.0 — confirm the MCP package LICENSE. Distinct from the already-seeded dennisgl playwright-scraper (screenshot-based).

candidates.intent: Automate Chrome/Chromium via Puppeteer to navigate, click, screenshot, and execute JavaScript, including attaching to existing browser windows.
candidates.input_contract: a URL or selector plus interaction commands
candidates.output_contract: rendered content, screenshots, or JS evaluation results
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A model cannot launch or attach to a Chrome instance or run page-context JavaScript on its own.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds Puppeteer-based browser control including connecting to existing Chrome windows for authenticated sessions.
candidates.verify_note: License not confirmed on listing. The original modelcontextprotocol/servers Puppeteer server is now archived (servers-archived).

candidates.intent: Let an AI app control the user's existing local browser tabs to automate navigation and interaction without a cloud service.
candidates.input_contract: a tab/target plus interaction steps
candidates.output_contract: page content and action results from the user's own browser
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A model cannot reach a user's logged-in local browser session to act on authenticated pages.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds local-browser automation that reuses the user's real session/cookies, avoiding re-auth and bot detection.
candidates.verify_note: License unverified on repo page; runs against the user's local browser — privacy/scope review required before any promotion.

candidates.intent: Search the web and scrape the top results into clean, retrieval-ready content in one call.
candidates.input_contract: a search query plus result-count/depth options
candidates.output_contract: top results scraped to Markdown/structured text with URLs
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A model cannot run a live search and fetch/clean multiple result pages for grounding.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds a one-shot search-then-scrape actor that returns cleaned source content with handles for RAG.
candidates.verify_note: Pre-configured actor surfaced by the Apify MCP server (MIT); requires Apify token and incurs per-run cost.

candidates.intent: Convert PDFs, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, HTML, and images into a structured DoclingDocument with layout, tables, and reading order.
candidates.input_contract: a document file or URL
candidates.output_contract: a DoclingDocument (Markdown/JSON) with layout, tables, and figures
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A text model cannot parse binary/visual document layout, recover reading order, or reconstruct tables from PDFs.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds IBM Research's deterministic document-conversion pipeline (layout + table structure) producing a typed document object.
candidates.verify_note: MIT per docling-project; companion Granite-Docling model is Apache-2.0 and adds model dependence for some steps.

candidates.intent: Expose Docling conversion and manipulation as MCP tools so agents can convert and query documents.
candidates.input_contract: a document file/URL plus a conversion or query request
candidates.output_contract: converted document content and structured fields via MCP tools
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A model has no built-in document-conversion engine to call as a tool.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds an MCP wrapper over Docling so an agent can convert and inspect documents with source handles.
candidates.verify_note: Part of docling-project (MIT). Confirm tool surface on the docling-mcp repo before relying.

candidates.intent: Extract text from programmatic PDFs together with precise character/word bounding-box coordinates.
candidates.input_contract: a programmatic (text-based) PDF
candidates.output_contract: text tokens with coordinates and page geometry
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A model cannot recover the exact spatial positions of text needed for layout-aware extraction.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds a deterministic PDF backend returning text with coordinates, enabling layout reconstruction and citation anchoring.
candidates.verify_note: MIT per docling-project; handles programmatic PDFs (not scanned images — pair with OCR for those).

candidates.intent: Parse complex PDFs/PPTX/DOCX/XLSX/HTML (tables, weird layouts, visuals) into LLM-ready Markdown/JSON via a GenAI-native parser.
candidates.input_contract: a document file plus parsing mode/instructions
candidates.output_contract: Markdown or JSON with reconstructed tables and structure
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A model cannot reliably reconstruct tables and complex layouts from binary documents on its own.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds LlamaCloud's hosted GenAI parser exposed over MCP for high-fidelity document-to-Markdown conversion.
candidates.verify_note: Hosted service (OAuth via LlamaCloud), not local; repo license unverified. Parsing quality is model-assisted, so output is not fully deterministic.

candidates.intent: Parse documents into clean structured text with a fast open-source parser.
candidates.input_contract: a document file (e.g. PDF/office formats)
candidates.output_contract: structured/cleaned text output
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A model lacks a local parser for turning binary documents into clean text.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds an open-source, self-hostable document parser as a deterministic preprocessing step.
candidates.verify_note: Described as open-source by run-llama; confirm exact SPDX license and format coverage on the repo.

candidates.intent: Partition diverse documents (PDF, HTML, Word, email, images) into typed elements (titles, narrative text, tables) with optional Tesseract OCR.
candidates.input_contract: a document file plus partition strategy options
candidates.output_contract: a list of typed document elements with metadata
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A model cannot detect element types or partition mixed-format documents into clean, typed chunks.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds an open-source ETL layer that partitions, chunks, and OCRs documents into structured elements for retrieval.
candidates.verify_note: Apache-2.0 confirmed via repo fetch; hi_res strategy invokes models, lowering full determinism. Enterprise Platform is separate/commercial.

candidates.intent: Run layout-detection and table/structure inference models used by the Unstructured partitioning pipeline.
candidates.input_contract: a document page image
candidates.output_contract: detected layout regions and table structures
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A text model cannot detect page-layout regions or table grids from a rendered page image.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds vision layout/table models that feed deterministic downstream extraction.
candidates.verify_note: Model-backed inference (Apache-2.0 per Unstructured-IO); output varies with model and image quality.

candidates.intent: Convert PDFs (and other docs) to high-quality Markdown/JSON, including equations, tables, and figures.
candidates.input_contract: a PDF (or supported document) and conversion options
candidates.output_contract: Markdown or JSON with equations, tables, and images
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A model cannot convert visually complex scientific PDFs (equations, multi-column, tables) into faithful Markdown.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds a high-accuracy PDF-to-Markdown converter optimized for books and scientific papers.
candidates.verify_note: GPL-3.0-or-later code; model weights are cc-by-nc-sa-4.0 with a sub-$5M revenue/funding waiver — licensing review required before commercial use.

candidates.intent: Extract and re-structure scholarly PDFs into TEI/XML: title, authors, affiliations, references, sections, and citations.
candidates.input_contract: a scientific/technical PDF
candidates.output_contract: TEI/XML with fine-grained bibliographic and full-text structure
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A model cannot reliably parse reference lists, affiliations, and metadata from arbitrary paper PDFs without fabricating fields.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds an ML system specialized for scholarly metadata/citation extraction with 68 fine-grained labels and TEI output.
candidates.verify_note: Apache-2.0 (docs CC-0, data CC-BY) per repo; the allenai/grobid fork exists for AI2 pipelines.

candidates.intent: Detect and extract text and metadata from over a thousand file types (PDF, Office, OpenDocument, HTML, images, audio, archives) through one interface.
candidates.input_contract: a file of any supported type
candidates.output_contract: extracted text plus detected metadata and MIME type
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A model cannot decode binary file formats or detect MIME types to pull text/metadata out of them.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds a universal, deterministic text+metadata extractor with a REST server, Java library, and CLI.
candidates.verify_note: Apache-2.0 (with separately-licensed subcomponents noted in LICENSE.txt). OCR requires bundling Tesseract.

candidates.intent: Extract precise per-character, line, rectangle, and table data from text-based PDFs.
candidates.input_contract: a text-based PDF and optional table-detection settings
candidates.output_contract: characters/lines with coordinates and extracted tables
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A model cannot access the low-level PDF object geometry needed to extract exact tables and char positions.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds deterministic, fine-grained PDF inspection and table extraction with full coordinate detail.
candidates.verify_note: MIT per repo. Text-based PDFs only — scanned pages need OCR first.

candidates.intent: Extract tabular data from text-based PDFs using lattice/stream/hybrid (and optional neural) parsers.
candidates.input_contract: a text-based PDF plus pages and flavor selection
candidates.output_contract: extracted tables as DataFrames/CSV with accuracy metrics
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A model cannot reliably reconstruct ruled or whitespace-delimited tables from PDF coordinates.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds multiple deterministic table parsers (lattice/stream/hybrid) with an auto flavor and accuracy reporting.
candidates.verify_note: MIT per camelot-dev. Text-based PDFs only; the optional neural parser adds a model dependency.

candidates.intent: Run open-source OCR to convert scanned images/PDF pages into machine-readable text across 100+ languages.
candidates.input_contract: an image or rasterized page plus language/PSM options
candidates.output_contract: recognized text (optionally with word/box coordinates or hOCR)
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A text model cannot read pixels — scanned documents have no extractable text without OCR.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds a mature, deterministic, fully local OCR engine with multilingual support and positional output.
candidates.verify_note: Apache-2.0 per repo. Accuracy depends on image quality/preprocessing; layout reconstruction is out of scope.

candidates.intent: Extract text from natural-scene images and documents across 80+ languages and scripts.
candidates.input_contract: an image plus a language list
candidates.output_contract: recognized text segments with bounding boxes and confidence
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A model cannot read text embedded in images, especially scene text across many scripts.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds a ready-to-use OCR with broad script coverage (Latin, Chinese, Arabic, Devanagari, Cyrillic) and box/confidence output.
candidates.verify_note: Apache-2.0 per repo LICENSE. Deep-learning OCR — output varies with image quality and language pack.

candidates.intent: Run multilingual OCR plus layout analysis and table recognition (PP-StructureV3) to turn PDFs/images into Markdown/JSON preserving structure.
candidates.input_contract: a PDF or image and a recognition/structure mode
candidates.output_contract: recognized text plus layout regions and reconstructed tables as Markdown/JSON
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A model cannot OCR, detect layout, and rebuild tables from scanned/complex documents simultaneously.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds an end-to-end OCR+layout+table toolkit (100+ languages) emitting structure-preserving Markdown/JSON.
candidates.verify_note: Apache-2.0 per project. Model-backed (varies with image quality); heavier runtime dependency (PaddlePaddle).

candidates.intent: Linearize PDFs (including tables, equations, handwriting) into reading-order plain text for LLM datasets using a vision-language model.
candidates.input_contract: a PDF (local or S3) plus batch/output configuration
candidates.output_contract: linearized plain text preserving reading order
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A model cannot, in one pass, OCR and reorder complex multi-column PDFs into faithful reading-order text at scale.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds an open VLM-based pipeline that linearizes large PDF corpora (incl. equations/handwriting) with S3 batch support.
candidates.verify_note: Apache-2.0 toolkit per repo; uses the olmOCR-2-7B VLM, so output is model-dependent (not fully deterministic). Needs a GPU/inference backend.

candidates.intent: Parse a UI screenshot into a structured list of interactable regions and icon/function captions for vision-based GUI agents.
candidates.input_contract: a UI screenshot image
candidates.output_contract: structured elements with bounding boxes, captions, and interactable flags
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A model grounding actions on a screenshot cannot reliably localize and label interactable UI elements alone.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds a screen-parsing module that converts screenshots into structured, grounded element lists for GUI agents.
candidates.verify_note: Repo license not confirmed here (model weights on HF have their own terms); model-backed detection — verify SPDX before relying.

candidates.intent: Parse complex documents (financial tables, forms, mixed-language) using layout detection plus an agentic OCR correction pass, and extract structured JSON by schema.
candidates.input_contract: a document file/URL plus an optional extraction schema or split/classify request
candidates.output_contract: structured text, tables, figures, or schema-conformant JSON
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A model alone cannot reliably parse visually dense financial tables/forms or self-correct OCR errors.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds a multi-pass parse+extract+split+classify API (over MCP) tuned for hard documents with structured output.
candidates.verify_note: Hosted commercial API (login via uvx mcp-server-reducto); SDK repo license unverified. Parsing is model-assisted, not fully deterministic.

candidates.intent: Extract ordered interleaved text and images from PDFs/images, reconstructing tables (HTML), equations (LaTeX), and layout into Markdown/JSON.
candidates.input_contract: a PDF or image
candidates.output_contract: Markdown with reconstructed tables/equations plus optional structured JSON
candidates.source_name: Mistral Document AI / Mistral OCR (la Plateforme API)
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A model cannot natively OCR complex multimodal documents while preserving tables, math, and reading order.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds a high-accuracy document-understanding API producing structured Markdown/JSON suitable for multimodal RAG.
candidates.verify_note: Hosted commercial API (Mistral la Plateforme; also on Vertex/Azure Foundry). No standalone MCP/repo confirmed; output is model-generated. Source is the vendor announcement page.

candidates.intent: Extract text, key-value pairs, tables, and form data from scanned documents via Amazon Textract.
candidates.input_contract: a document image/PDF (or S3 reference) plus analysis feature flags
candidates.output_contract: structured blocks: text, tables, forms, and key-value pairs with geometry
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A model cannot OCR scanned forms or recover key-value/table relationships from document images.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds a typed Python wrapper over Textract for parsing responses, drawing boxes, and exporting structured forms/tables.
candidates.verify_note: Wrapper is aws-samples (Apache-2.0 typical for that org — confirm); calls the paid Textract API. Recognition quality varies with scan quality.

candidates.intent: Analyze documents with Azure Document Intelligence (prebuilt + custom models) to extract layout, tables, key-value pairs, and document fields.
candidates.input_contract: a document file/URL plus a model id (prebuilt or custom)
candidates.output_contract: structured fields, tables, and layout with confidence scores
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A model cannot run document-layout/field extraction models or apply trained custom extractors on its own.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds Azure Document Intelligence document understanding exposed over MCP (Streamable HTTP) combined with LLM reasoning.
candidates.verify_note: ARGUS sample (license unconfirmed) wraps the paid Azure Document Intelligence + GPT; verify SPDX and separate the deterministic extraction from LLM steps.

candidates.intent: Analyze multimodal content (documents, images, audio, video) via Azure Content Understanding exposed as MCP tools.
candidates.input_contract: a content file plus an analyzer/schema selection
candidates.output_contract: structured analysis fields per the selected analyzer
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A model cannot directly invoke a managed multimodal-analysis service to produce schema-conformant fields.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds an MCP server over Azure Content Understanding for structured extraction across content modalities.
candidates.verify_note: Azure sample (license unconfirmed) over a paid service; extraction is model-backed. Confirm SPDX and scope before relying.

candidates.intent: Combine Azure Document Intelligence extraction with GPT reasoning to understand and answer over uploaded documents.
candidates.input_contract: a document upload plus a question or extraction request
candidates.output_contract: extracted fields plus a grounded answer/summary
candidates.gap_hypothesis: Document QA needs both precise field extraction and reasoning; a bare model lacks the extraction half and hallucinates fields.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds a pipeline that grounds GPT answers in Azure Document Intelligence extractions, reducing fabricated values.
candidates.verify_note: Sample app; the reasoning layer is non-deterministic. Only the extraction step is deterministic. License unverified.

candidates.intent: Classify a document into a category (e.g. invoice, contract, form) before routing to extraction.
candidates.input_contract: a document file/URL plus candidate categories
candidates.output_contract: a predicted category with confidence
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A model alone classifies documents inconsistently from raw text and lacks layout signals.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds a layout-aware document classifier that routes inputs to the right extraction path deterministically by API.
candidates.verify_note: Tool surfaced by the Reducto MCP server; hosted commercial API, SDK license unverified.

candidates.intent: Segment a long document into labeled sections (e.g. by document type within a packet).
candidates.input_contract: a multi-document PDF/packet
candidates.output_contract: labeled page ranges/sections
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A model cannot reliably detect document boundaries inside a merged multi-doc PDF.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds deterministic-by-API document splitting so each segment is parsed/extracted correctly.
candidates.verify_note: Tool surfaced by the Reducto MCP server; hosted commercial API, SDK license unverified.

candidates.intent: Run a self-hosted HTTP API of Microsoft OmniParser to convert screenshots into structured UI element descriptions.
candidates.input_contract: a screenshot via an HTTP request
candidates.output_contract: structured element list (boxes, captions, interactable flags)
candidates.gap_hypothesis: Teams need OmniParser as a callable service, which the base research repo does not provide out of the box.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds a self-hosted API wrapper so agents can call screen-parsing over HTTP without managing the model directly.
candidates.verify_note: Community wrapper; license unverified and inherits OmniParser's model terms. Model-backed output.

candidates.intent: Call Docling document conversion through a FastAPI REST service.
candidates.input_contract: a document file/URL via a REST request plus conversion options
candidates.output_contract: converted DoclingDocument (Markdown/JSON) over HTTP
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A model cannot host or call a document-conversion service without a server wrapper.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds a deployable REST front end for Docling so pipelines and agents can convert documents over HTTP.
candidates.verify_note: MIT per docling-project; confirm endpoint surface on the docling-serve repo.

candidates.intent: Ingest and preprocess batches of documents from many sources into structured, chunked elements for downstream loading.
candidates.input_contract: a source connector config plus partition/chunk settings
candidates.output_contract: batches of structured elements ready for embedding/loading
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A model cannot orchestrate multi-source batch ingestion, partitioning, and chunking at scale.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds a connector-driven batch pipeline that turns document corpora into structured, chunked rows.
candidates.verify_note: Apache-2.0 (same repo). hi_res/model steps reduce determinism; enterprise connectors may be separate.

candidates.intent: Extract tabular data from PDFs through a web UI powered by Camelot.
candidates.input_contract: a PDF uploaded via the web interface plus page/region selection
candidates.output_contract: extracted tables downloadable as CSV/Excel
candidates.gap_hypothesis: Non-programmatic table extraction needs an interactive tool a model cannot provide.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds a Camelot-backed web UI for human-in-the-loop PDF table extraction with deterministic export.
candidates.verify_note: MIT per camelot-dev. Text-based PDFs only; interactive workflow.

candidates.intent: Process the same document through multiple AWS engines (Textract, Bedrock, BDA) and compare OCR/extraction outputs.
candidates.input_contract: a document plus the set of engines to run
candidates.output_contract: per-engine extraction results for side-by-side comparison
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A model cannot run or benchmark multiple managed OCR engines to pick the best for a document.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds a comparison harness across Textract/Bedrock/BDA so the strongest extractor can be selected with evidence.
candidates.verify_note: aws-samples (license unconfirmed); calls paid AWS services. Useful as an evaluation/selection scaffold.

candidates.intent: Learn extraction rules from a few annotated example pages and apply them to scrape similarly-structured pages.
candidates.input_contract: example HTML pages with annotated target fields
candidates.output_contract: extracted field values from new pages of the same template
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A model cannot derive a stable, reusable extractor from examples without re-reasoning over every page.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds template-induction extraction that generalizes from a few labeled pages to a whole site section.
candidates.verify_note: Maintained under scrapy org; confirm SPDX on repo. Works on similarly-structured HTML.

candidates.intent: Benchmark document-parsing accuracy across parsers/configurations using a published evaluation harness.
candidates.input_contract: a labeled document set plus parser configs
candidates.output_contract: accuracy/comparison metrics across parsers
candidates.gap_hypothesis: Choosing a parser by feel is unreliable; a model cannot measure parser accuracy without a harness.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds a reproducible benchmark to evaluate parsing quality and justify parser selection with evidence.
candidates.verify_note: Vendor-published benchmark (potential bias); license unverified. Treat results as a starting point, re-run independently.

candidates.intent: Extract text from a document via a lightweight serverless wrapper around Apache Tika.
candidates.input_contract: a document file (e.g. via a function call)
candidates.output_contract: extracted plain text
candidates.gap_hypothesis: Running Tika as a managed/serverless text extractor needs a wrapper a model cannot supply.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds a small deployable wrapper that exposes Tika text extraction as a simple callable.
candidates.verify_note: Third-party wrapper; license unverified. Inherits Tika (Apache-2.0) behavior.

candidates.intent: Convert Office docs, PDFs, HTML, CSV/JSON/XML, images, audio, and ZIPs into structure-preserving Markdown for LLM consumption.
candidates.input_contract: a supported file path or stream
candidates.output_contract: Markdown preserving headings, tables, and lists
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A model cannot decode 12+ binary/structured formats into clean Markdown that preserves semantic structure.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds a deterministic, broad-format file-to-Markdown converter (with a CLI and MCP option) for retrieval pipelines.
candidates.verify_note: MIT per repo (Microsoft AutoGen team). Image/audio handling can invoke models, lowering determinism for those types.

candidates.intent: Run OCR, line/layout detection, reading-order, and table recognition across 90+ languages.
candidates.input_contract: a document image or PDF page plus a language hint
candidates.output_contract: recognized text with lines, layout regions, reading order, and tables
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A model cannot OCR, detect layout, and infer reading order across many scripts from a page image.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds a multilingual OCR+layout+reading-order+table toolkit for faithful document structuring.
candidates.verify_note: Code Apache-2.0; model weights under a modified AI-Pubs OpenRAIL-M (free under $5M funding/revenue) — license review needed. pyproject lists GPL-3.0, conflicting with the README; confirm.

candidates.intent: OCR and extract documents to Markdown by rasterizing pages and prompting a vision model page-by-page.
candidates.input_contract: a PDF/DOCX/image plus a chosen vision model and credentials
candidates.output_contract: aggregated Markdown across pages
candidates.gap_hypothesis: Plain text models cannot read page images; getting Markdown from scanned/complex docs needs a vision OCR loop.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds a provider-agnostic vision-OCR pipeline (OpenAI/Azure/Anthropic/Bedrock) that returns aggregated Markdown.
candidates.verify_note: MIT code, but output is fully VLM-generated (non-deterministic) and depends on a paid vision model — treat as model-assisted, never a truth source.

candidates.intent: Extract text/images/metadata and render, convert, and manipulate PDFs (and other formats) at high speed with low-level control.
candidates.input_contract: a PDF (or supported document) plus extraction/manipulation operations
candidates.output_contract: extracted text/images/metadata or a modified document
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A model cannot read PDF object structure or render/manipulate pages to extract precise text, images, and geometry.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds a fast MuPDF-backed library for deterministic extraction, rendering, and manipulation of documents.
candidates.verify_note: AGPL-3.0 (commercial license available from Artifex) — copyleft review required before bundling into a closed product.

candidates.intent: Extract PDFs into RAG-ready Markdown/JSON with layout-aware multi-column handling, table detection, and selective OCR.
candidates.input_contract: a PDF plus output-format/OCR options
candidates.output_contract: Markdown, JSON, or plain text with tables and structure
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A model cannot turn multi-column PDFs with tables into clean, chunk-ready Markdown on its own.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds a PyMuPDF layer tuned for LLM ingestion (layout-aware Markdown, table detection, region-selective OCR).
candidates.verify_note: Dual-licensed AGPL-3.0 / commercial. Selective-OCR step adds model dependence; copyleft review required.

candidates.intent: Convert scientific PDFs (LaTeX math, tables) into a Mathpix-Markdown (.mmd) representation via a neural OCR model.
candidates.input_contract: an academic/scientific PDF
candidates.output_contract: a .mmd file with LaTeX math and tables
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A model cannot reliably recover LaTeX equations and table structure from rendered paper PDFs.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds a neural academic-document parser that emits math-aware Markdown for scientific corpora.
candidates.verify_note: MIT code (FAIR); output is model-generated (not deterministic) and best on academic layouts. Needs a GPU for speed.

candidates.intent: Run a unified end-to-end OCR-2.0 model over text, formulas, tables, charts, and sheet music.
candidates.input_contract: a document/image plus an OCR task mode
candidates.output_contract: recognized content (plain text, formatted text, or formula/table markup)
candidates.gap_hypothesis: Heterogeneous OCR (formulas, charts, sheet music) exceeds what a text model can read from images.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds a single end-to-end OCR-2.0 model spanning many content types in one interface.
candidates.verify_note: RESEARCH-USE-ONLY license (follows Vary's terms) — NOT cleared for commercial use; model-generated output. Confirm before any promotion.

candidates.intent: Download web pages and extract the main text, metadata, and comments, stripping boilerplate, to TXT/Markdown/JSON/XML-TEI.
candidates.input_contract: a URL or raw HTML plus output-format options
candidates.output_contract: main text plus metadata in the chosen format
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A model cannot reliably separate article body from navigation/ads/boilerplate across heterogeneous pages.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds a precision/recall-balanced main-text extractor (Readability-derived) with multi-format output for clean corpora.
candidates.verify_note: Apache-2.0 since v1.8.0 (earlier GPLv3+). Deterministic heuristic extraction; quality varies by page structure.

candidates.intent: Fetch and scrape pages through a managed API that handles headless rendering, proxy rotation, geotargeting, and CAPTCHAs.
candidates.input_contract: a target URL plus options (JS rendering, premium/geo proxy, custom JS, extraction rules)
candidates.output_contract: rendered HTML or extracted data
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A model cannot rotate proxies, solve CAPTCHAs, or render JS at scale to retrieve protected pages.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds a managed scraping API (with an MCP option) that returns rendered/extracted content despite anti-bot measures.
candidates.verify_note: SDK license unverified on repo; paid API. A community MCP (igormidev/scrapping_bee_mcp) and an official mcp.scrapingbee.com also exist.
